Our Story

A home first,
a restaurant second

Before it was a café, 113 Wagner Road was home to the Pantaleon family — Mama, her seven children, and two dogs — tucked along a pine-shaded street in Military Cut-Off. The children eventually convinced their mother to open the gate and share the table she had always set so well.

The garden, shaped by landscape artist Kiko Villalba, begins with narrow steps that make you slow down. Inside, Chef Rudolph Peter Cabuay — who once cooked for big-city palates at Aubergine in BGC — plates comfort food with a fine hand: food for sharing, meant to feed hearts, not just stomachs.

There are no walk-ins and no rush. Just fifty-five seats, a garden that glows after dark, and a meal that unfolds one course at a time.

— Welcome home.

Proposals · Anniversaries · Slow Celebrations

Baguio's unofficial engagement capital — a garden where time seems to pause.

More proposals have been whispered in this garden than we can count. Tell us what you're celebrating when you reserve, and the house will help you make it unforgettable — a quiet corner, candlelight, and dessert at exactly the right moment.

Reservations

Every table is
by reservation

We keep the gate closed to walk-ins so every seating stays unhurried. Here's how a table becomes yours.

01

Send a request

Pick your date, seating, and set menu. We ask at least three days ahead — weekends go first.

02

We confirm by email

The house replies with your seating time, the day's courses, and anything we should prepare for your occasion.

03

Come hungry, stay dreamy

The gate opens for your seating. Your table is set in the garden, and the courses begin when you're ready.

Good to know
before you book

  • 55 seats at most — when the garden is full, we stop taking names.
  • Brunch runs two seatings: 9:00–11:00 AM and 11:30 AM–1:30 PM.
  • Dinner guests are welcomed at the gate from 5:00 PM.
  • Celebrating something? Mention it — proposals are our love language.
  • Baguio cools fast after dark; a wrap or jacket is a good idea.
